opportunities.title: APEX Awards

amount.raw: Applicants can apply for up to £200,000

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Established independent researchers with a strong track record, holding a permanent or fixed-term position, based in a UK University or UK not-for-profit research organisation. Lead applicant may include up to two Co-applicants from a different Academy remit.
opportunities.summary: APEX Awards (Academies Partnership in Supporting Excellence in Cross-disciplinary research) offer established independent researchers the opportunity to pursue genuine interdisciplinary and curiosity-driven research across the boundary between science, engineering, and the social sciences and humanities, in partnership with the British Academy, Royal Society and Royal Academy of Engineering.

opportunities.title: SHAPE Involve and Engage
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Any researcher based in the UK who meets the conditions of the call, across career stages. Previous successful recipients of this award are not eligible to reapply.
opportunities.summary: Public engagement programme supporting ambitious projects to engage the public with the humanities and social sciences, working in partnership with a gallery, archive, library, museum (GLAM) or performing arts organisation.

opportunities.title: The Alexander von Humboldt Foundation and The British Academy Knowledge Frontiers Symposium 2027

amount.raw: Symposium covers travel, accommodation, and visa costs; seed funding available for collaborations

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early career researchers in the humanities and social sciences affiliated with research institutions in the UK or Germany.
opportunities.summary: Call for early career researchers to attend a research collaboration symposium on the theme 'Humans and Nature: More resilient towards the future', bringing together around 15 UK and 15 German early career researchers to encourage collaboration and networking, with seed funding available for international collaborations.

opportunities.title: Postdoctoral Fellowships

amount.raw: Three year award; 80% of salary costs, directly allocated and indirect costs under FEC

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early-career researchers in the humanities and social sciences based at an eligible UK university or research organisation. British citizens, EEA nationals, anyone with a UK doctorate, or those with strong prior association with the UK. Must have completed viva between 1 April 2024 and 1 April 2027 and not hold a permanent academic post.
opportunities.summary: Three-year fellowship for outstanding early-career researchers in the humanities or social sciences to pursue an independent research project towards completion of a significant piece of publishable research, funded by DSIT.

opportunities.title: Talent Development Awards 2026-27
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Established researchers in the humanities and social sciences ordinarily resident in the UK, holding a current long-term appointment at a UK-based HEI or IRO for the full duration of the award.
opportunities.summary: Scheme to promote the acquisition and advancement of skills (quantitative skills, data science, digital humanities, languages) by UK-based researchers, supporting innovative research methods through skills development, collaboration or dissemination.

opportunities.title: International Interdisciplinary Research Projects 2027

amount.raw: Up to £300,000 over 2 years (80% FEC; total project value at 100% FEC up to £375,000)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Principal Investigator must be a researcher from the humanities and social sciences based at an eligible UK university or research institute, of postdoctoral or above status, spending at least 20% time on the award. Co-applicants based overseas required.
opportunities.summary: International Interdisciplinary Research programme supporting projects led by UK-based researchers in the humanities and social sciences working with international partners on genuinely interdisciplinary projects across SHAPE and STEM disciplines on the theme of Mobilities.

opportunities.title: Global Innovation Fellowships: The German Council on Foreign Relations (DGAP) 2026-27

amount.raw: Up to £150,000 for 12 months (with Full Economic Costing at 80 per cent)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK-based early- and mid-career researchers from across the humanities and social sciences.
opportunities.summary: Global Innovation Fellowships provide UK-based early- and mid-career researchers in the humanities and social sciences the opportunity to develop skills, networks and careers by embedding in the office of the German Council on Foreign Relations (DGAP) in Berlin, producing policy-relevant analysis.

opportunities.title: Additional Needs

amount.raw: Funding of up to £4,000 (exceptional circumstances above £4,000 considered)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Current British Academy award-holders on any scheme, or applicants intending to apply for a British Academy award in the next six months who need support with their application.
opportunities.summary: Specific funding to support additional needs that applicants and award-holders may require (e.g. equipment to overcome barriers to disabled researchers, caring costs for research trips, assistance for applicants requiring support to make an application). Offered on a rolling basis and reviewed monthly.

opportunities.title: British Academy/Leverhulme Small Research Grants

amount.raw: Up to £10,000 in value, tenable for up to 24 months

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Postdoctoral scholars (or equivalent) ordinarily resident in the United Kingdom. Applications require approval of the employing institution; independent scholars eligible. Co-applicants may be from anywhere, but the Principal Applicant must be ordinarily resident in the UK.
opportunities.summary: The Academy's most popular scheme, providing awards up to £10,000 to cover the cost of expenses arising from a defined research project, tenable for 1-24 months. Funded as a public-private partnership including DSIT, Leverhulme Trust and Wellcome Trust.
